translation.note: Latin at farmer1998:21862-21866 and corollary at 21869-21870 match. Sense agrees with Farmer's English at 21910-21916 (sense only) in construing the preamble: Pico would assert firmly were the theologians' common way of speaking not opposed. 'praecise' as 'exactly and only' follows copenhaver2022:10776-10777 and is declared. 'quando placet' / 'quando sibi placet' both 'when he likes': no loss. Qualifiers 'probabiliter', 'in se', 'praecise' all kept. Copenhaver's rendering of the preamble ('I would assert the opposite firmly', 10139) differs from Farmer's and the entry's; see adjudication.

corrections.old: The thesis turns on the difference between assent and assertion: to assent is to accept a proposition, while to assert is to put it forward as one's own claim, and Pico here asserts only that his dictum is probable (copenhaver2022:5735-5740, 5753-5755; farmer1998:21862-21864).

for_human_adjudication: Latinist: the preamble 'nisi esset communis modus dicendi theologorum in oppositum, firmiter assererem'. The entry and Farmer read 'in oppositum' with the theologians' manner of speaking (Pico would assert his dictum firmly); Copenhaver renders 'I would assert the opposite firmly except that theologians generally say it that way' (copenhaver2022:10139-10140). The entry's translation_note 2 sides with Farmer.

Historian: whether the commission censured 4>18 with its corollary (Pico's report, copenhaver2022:11515-11516; Farmer 21895-21896) or the corollary alone (Blum's list, dougherty2008:2208-2211). The entry records both without deciding; Dorez and Thuasne p. 129 is not in the corpus.
